safety_verdicts.content: Patient is taking the Clenil inhaler every day, 2 puffs twice daily.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated notes Clenil used daily (section-010) but does not capture the baseline regimen '2 puffs twice daily'.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the baseline Clenil regimen (2 puffs twice daily) reduces accuracy when assessing control and deciding how much to step up inhaled corticosteroid dosing during an exacerbation. This could lead to inappropriate dose adjustments or less effective follow-up planning, but is unlikely to directly cause severe harm on its own.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient has had asthma since childhood.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated lists asthma but does not specify 'since childhood' (section-018 lacks duration/onset).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not specifying that asthma has been present since childhood is primarily a loss of clinical context and usually does not change immediate management of an acute mild exacerbation. The diagnosis of asthma is still captured, so the omission is unlikely to alter treatment decisions meaningfully.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient has never needed antibiotics or steroids for asthma.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated only states no oral steroids/antibiotics at the time of last attack (section-012) and does not clearly state the broader gold concept 'never needed antibiotics or steroids for asthma'.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failing to clearly document that the patient has never needed antibiotics or steroids for asthma may distort perceived historical severity and could influence future clinicians’ threshold for prescribing systemic steroids or antibiotics. This is more likely to cause unnecessary treatment or monitoring rather than major injury.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient routinely uses the Clenil inhaler, 2 puffs twice daily.

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting the maintenance dose/frequency of Clenil (2 puffs twice daily) can impair medication reconciliation and safe step-up/step-down decisions, especially when advising to increase to 4 puffs twice daily. The likely impact is suboptimal dosing decisions or added follow-up needs rather than severe harm.
